list_timezones.description: Get timezones. Returns the cities Cal.com knows a timezone for, as a `city` to show the user and the IANA `timezone` to store and to send back to Cal.com. Without `search` every city is returned, around 7000 of them. `search` searches the full source dataset by city name and additionally matches timezone names, so a search for an abbreviation such as `PDT` resolves to `{ "city": "Pacific Time - US & Canada", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles" }`. City and alias names match by case-insensitive substring; complete IANA identifiers also match by case-insensitive equality. Partial IANA identifiers are not matched; timezone matches come first, then cities ordered by population, so the most likely answer is first. City results include `country` and `region` to distinguish same-named cities. Each city name and timezone pair appears once; display the location fields alongside the city and let the user choose. Timezone entries have no `pop`, `country` or `region`. Cal.com stores the IANA identifier, never an abbreviation or an offset: `America/Los_Angeles` already means PDT in summer and PST in winter, and the response has no offset to interpret.

search.description: Match city or timezone names by case-insensitive substring, or a complete IANA timezone identifier by case-insensitive equality. Omit it to get every city. Example: PDT.

limit.description: Return at most this many entries (a whole number from 1 to 250). Results are ordered by relevance, so a limit keeps the entries a user is most likely to want. Omit it to get every match. Example: 20.

create.description: Create a booking. POST /v2/bookings is used to create regular bookings, recurring bookings and instant bookings. The request bodies for all 3 are almost the same except: If eventTypeId in the request body is id of a regular event, then regular booking is created. If it is an id of a recurring event type, then recurring booking is created. Meaning that the request bodies are equal but the outcome depends on what kind of event type it is with the goal of making it as seamless for developers as possible. For team event types it is possible to create instant meeting. To do that just pass `"instant": true` to the requ... Cal.com enforces the body variants. Regular booking (regular event type or dynamic booking via usernames) requires start, attendee. Instant booking (instant=true) requires attendee, instant. Recurring booking (recurring event type) requires start, attendee. usernames must contain distinct items. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields. location has Cal.com-validated object variants. Published nullable fields cannot be cleared to null through this connector. Accepts different types of booking input: Standard Booking, Instant Booking, or Recurring Booking.

name.description: The name of the attendee. Example: John Doe.

timeZone.description: The time zone of the attendee. Example: America/New_York.

phoneNumber.description: The phone number of the attendee in international format. Example: +919876543210.

language.description: The preferred language of the attendee. Used for booking confirmation. Default: en. Example: it.

email.description: The email of the attendee. Example: john.doe@example.com.

bookingFieldsResponses.description: Booking field responses consisting of an object with booking field slug as keys and user response as values for custom booking fields added by you. Cal.com validates the keys and values of this object. Example: {"customField":"customValue"}.

leadEnrichmentOptOut.description: The booker's answer to the lead enrichment opt-out, for an event type with a workflow that looks bookers up with lead enrichment. Send `true` when the booker ticked the opt-out and `false` when they were shown it and left it unticked. Sending `false` asserts that the booker saw the opt-out. Leave it out when the booker was not shown it: a booking without an answer is never looked up. Example: false.

eventTypeId.description: The ID of the event type that is booked. Required unless eventTypeSlug and username are provided as an alternative to identifying the event type. Example: 123.

eventTypeSlug.description: The slug of the event type. Required along with username / teamSlug and optionally organizationSlug if eventTypeId is not provided. Example: my-event-type.

username.description: The username of the event owner. Required along with eventTypeSlug and optionally organizationSlug if eventTypeId is not provided. Example: john-doe.

teamSlug.description: Team slug for team that owns event type for which slots are fetched. Required along with eventTypeSlug and optionally organizationSlug if the team is part of organization Example: john-doe.

organizationSlug.description: The organization slug. Optional, only used when booking with eventTypeSlug + username, eventTypeSlug + teamSlug, or usernames. Example: acme-corp.

usernames.description: Usernames of the hosts for a dynamic group booking (no stored event type) - every listed user must be available. Must contain 2 to 20 distinct usernames, and can't be combined with eventTypeId, eventTypeSlug, username or teamSlug. Pass organizationSlug when the users belong to an organization; without it only users outside any organization are found. Platform managed users can only be booked with their own OAuth client's credentials or one of its access tokens; to any other request they are reported as not found. Duration defaults to 30 minutes and can be changed with lengthInMinutes (15, 30, 45, 60 or 90). Cal.com requires distinct items. Example: ["alice","bob"].

hostUsernames.description: Only for collective event types: books just these hosts instead of every host. The organizer is whichever of them comes first in the event type's host order, not in this list. For a team in an organization, use the hosts' organization usernames. Fetch slots with the same hostUsernames first. Every username must be a host of the event type, otherwise the request fails with 400 and the message "invalid_hosts". At most 50 distinct usernames of at most 255 characters each. Leaving it out, or passing an empty list, books every host. Ignored for other event types and for dynamic group bookings (usernames). A seated or recurring collective event type refuses it with 400. Can't be sent with instant or recurrenceCount, and rescheduling a booking keeps the hosts of the original booking. Example: ["alice","bob"].

guests.description: An optional list of guest emails attending the event. Example: ["guest1@example.com","guest2@example.com"].

meetingUrl.description: Deprecated - use 'location' instead. Meeting URL just for this booking. Displayed in email and calendar event. If not provided then cal video link will be generated. Cal.com format: uri. Example: https://example.com/meeting.

location.description: One of the event type locations. If instead of passing one of the location objects as required by schema you are still passing a string please use an object. Cal.com variants: Address, Attendee Address, Attendee Defined, Attendee Phone, Integration, Link, Phone, Organizer Default App.

Team- and organization-scoped keys are restricted to events in their stored team or organization. Otherwise this parameter is silently ignored. Only supported on the 2026-02-25 and 2026-05-01 API versions. Example: true.

Only supported on the 2026-02-25 and 2026-05-01 API versions. Example: true.

The applied value is returned as instantMeetingExpiresInSeconds. Example: 120.

get_by_seat.description: Get a booking by seat UID. Get a seated booking by its seat reference UID. This is useful when you have a seatUid from a seated booking and want to retrieve the full booking details. Cancelled seats remain resolvable by the same seatUid: the parent booking is returned and the matching attendee is tagged with status `cancelled`. Only that attendee is listed — remaining live attendees are not mixed in. Occupied-seat counts on GET /bookings/:uid are unchanged. A seat reschedule that keeps the same seatUid still resolves from the live row. If you are fetching a seated booking for an event type with 'show attendees' disabled, then to retrieve attendees in the response either set 'show attendees' to true on event type level or you have to provide an authentication method of event type owner, host, team admin or owner or org admin or owner.

get.description: Get a booking. `:bookingUid` can be 1. uid of a normal booking 2. uid of one of the recurring booking recurrences 3. uid of recurring booking which will return an array of all recurring booking recurrences (stored as recurringBookingUid on one of the individual recurrences). If you are fetching a seated booking for an event type with 'show attendees' disabled, then to retrieve attendees in the response either set 'show attendees' to true on event type level or you have to provide an authentication method of event type owner, host, team admin or owner or org admin or owner.

get_recordings.description: Get all the recordings for the booking. Fetches all the recordings for the booking `:bookingUid`. Requires authentication and proper authorization. Access is granted to the booking organizer and hosts, and to team or organization members whose role can view the booking and has the `booking.readRecordings` permission, which team and organization admins and owners have by default.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_READ` scope is required.

get_transcripts.description: Get Cal Video real time transcript download links for the booking. Fetches all the transcript download links for the booking `:bookingUid`. Requires authentication and proper authorization. Access is granted to the booking organizer and hosts, and to team or organization members whose role can view the booking and has the `booking.readRecordings` permission, which team and organization admins and owners have by default.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_READ` scope is required.

reschedule.description: Reschedule a booking. Reschedule a booking or seated booking. Reschedulable booking statuses: - `accepted` — the confirmed booking is moved to the new start time. - `pending` — a booking awaiting host confirmation can be rescheduled. The new booking stays `pending` until the host confirms or declines it. Non-reschedulable booking statuses (endpoint responds with `400 Bad Request`): - `cancelled` —... Cal.com enforces the body variants. Regular or recurring booking (omit seatUid) requires start. Seated booking (supply seatUid) requires start, seatUid. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields. Accepts different types of reschedule booking input: Standard or Recurring Booking, or Seated Booking. If you're rescheduling a seated booking as org admin of booking host, pass booking input for Standard or Recurring Booking along with your access token in the request header. If you are rescheduling a seated booking for an event type with 'show attendees' disabled, then to retrieve attendees in the response either set 'show attendees' to true on event type level or you have to provide an authentication method of event type owner, host, team admin or owner or org admin or owner.

start.description: Start time in ISO 8601 format for the new booking Cal.com format: date-time. Example: 2024-08-13T10:00:00Z.

lengthInMinutes.description: If the event type has multiple possible lengths, you can pass the new booking length here. If not provided then the original booking length is kept. Example: 30.

If event type owner email is provided then rescheduled booking will be automatically confirmed. If attendee email or no email is passed then the event type owner will have to confirm the rescheduled booking.

reschedulingReason.description: Reason for rescheduling the booking Example: User requested reschedule.

rescheduleWithSameHost.description: Only for round robin event types that let the person rescheduling choose the host. True keeps the original host, false lets round robin pick from the whole team. Ignored for every other event type. Example: true.

Team- and organization-scoped keys are restricted to events in their stored team or organization. Otherwise this parameter is silently ignored. Only supported on the 2026-02-25 and 2026-05-01 API versions. Example: true.

Only supported on the 2026-02-25 and 2026-05-01 API versions. Example: true.

Team- and organization-scoped keys are restricted to events in their stored team or organization. Otherwise this parameter is silently ignored. Only supported on the 2026-02-25 and 2026-05-01 API versions. Example: true.

cancel.description: Cancel a booking. :bookingUid can be :bookingUid of an usual booking, individual recurrence or recurring booking to cancel all recurrences. Cancelling normal bookings: If the booking is not seated and not recurring, simply pass :bookingUid in the request URL `/bookings/:bookingUid/cancel` and optionally cancellationReason in the request body `{"cancellationReason": "Will travel"}`. Cancelling seated bookings: It is possible to cancel specific seat within a booking as an attendee or all of the seats as the host. 1. As an attendee - provide :bookingUid in the request URL `/bookings/:bookingUid/cancel` and seatUid in the request body `{"seatUid": "123-123-123"}` . This will remove this particular attendance from the booking. 2. As the host or org admin of host - host can cancel booking for all attendees aka for every seat, this also applies to org admins. Provide :bookingUid in... Cal.com enforces the body variants. Regular or recurring booking (omit seatUid) requires no body inputs. Seated booking (supply seatUid) requires seatUid. Accepts different types of cancel booking input: Standard or Recurring Booking (for normal or recurring bookings) or Seated Booking (for seated bookings).

cancelSubsequentBookings.description: For recurring non-seated booking only - if true, cancel booking with the bookingUid of the individual recurrence and all recurrences that come after it.

seatUid.description: Uid of the specific seat within booking. Example: 3be561a9-31f1-4b8e-aefc-9d9a085f0dd1.

mark_absent.description: Mark a booking absence. The provided authorization header refers to the owner of the booking.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_WRITE` scope is required.

host.description: Whether the host was absent Example: false.

reassign.description: Reassign a booking. Reassigns the host of a round robin or managed event type booking. The provided authorization header refers to the owner of the booking. Without `userUuid` in the body, an available round robin host is picked automatically. With `userUuid`, the booking is reassigned to that user. For a **round robin** booking, the user must be one of the booking's hosts and the booking keeps its `uid`. For a **managed event** booking, the user must be one of the users the managed event is assigned to — list them, along with their availability for the booking's slot, with `GET /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/reassignment-candidates`. Reassignment moves the booking onto the new host's own child event type, so the original booking is cancelled and **the returned booking has a new `uid`** which you must store in place of the old one. Recurring managed bookings cannot be reassigned yet.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_WRITE` scope is required. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields.

userUuid.description: UUID of the user to reassign the booking to. Omit it to let Cal.com pick an available round robin host. For a managed event booking, list the eligible users with `GET /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/reassignment-candidates` and pass a candidate's `uuid`. Cal.com format: uuid. Example: 3f2504e0-4f89-41d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301.

reason.description: Reason for reassigning the booking. Only recorded when `userUuid` is set. Example: Host has to take another call.

reassign_host.description: Reassign a booking to a specific host. Currently only supports reassigning host for round robin bookings. The provided authorization header refers to the owner of the booking.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_WRITE` scope is required.

reason.description: Reason for reassigning the booking Example: Host has to take another call.

confirm.description: Confirm a booking. The provided authorization header refers to the owner of the booking.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_WRITE` scope is required.

confirm_seats.description: Confirm booking seats. Confirm selected seats on a booking whose event type requires confirmation and has seats. The authorization header refers to a host who can update the booking. `confirmedSeatUids` lists seats that were waiting and are now confirmed. Seats that were already confirmed stay confirmed and are omitted. `POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/confirm` refuses these bookings. Pass each seat's `seatUid` here instead. Available with `cal-api-version` `2024-08-13`, `2026-02-25`, and `2026-05-01`. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_WRITE` scope is required.

seatUids.description: Seat UIDs to confirm. A seat that is already confirmed stays confirmed. Duplicate UIDs in one request are confirmed once. Example: ["3be561a9-31f1-4b8e-aefc-9d9a085f0dd1"].

decline_seats.description: Decline booking seats. Decline selected seats on a booking whose event type requires confirmation and has seats. The authorization header refers to a host who can update the booking. `declinedSeatUids` lists seats that were waiting or confirmed and are now declined. Seats that were already declined stay declined and are omitted. A confirmed seat can be declined. An optional `reason` is stored on each declined seat and included in its decline email and booking-rejected workflow. `POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/decline` refuses these bookings. Pass each seat's `seatUid` here instead. Available with `cal-api-version` `2024-08-13`, `2026-02-25`, and `2026-05-01`. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_WRITE` scope is required.

seatUids.description: Seat UIDs to decline. A waiting or confirmed seat becomes declined. A seat that is already declined stays declined. Duplicate UIDs in one request are declined once. Example: ["3be561a9-31f1-4b8e-aefc-9d9a085f0dd1"].

get_calendar_links.description: Get 'Add to Calendar' links for a booking. Retrieve calendar links for a booking that can be used to add the event to various calendar services. get_references.description: Get booking references. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_READ` scope is required.

verify_email.description: Verify email with code. Verifies an email address using the one-time code that was previously sent. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields.

list_attendees.description: Get all attendees for a booking. Retrieve all attendees for a specific booking by its UID.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_READ` scope is required.

items.description: Cal.com format: uuid.

contactIds.description: Ids of the authenticated user's own contacts, from `GET /v2/contacts`. get_routing_trace.description: Get the routing trace for a booking. Retrieve the step-by-step routing trace for a booking identified by its UID. Shows how the booking was routed through routing forms, CRM lookups, and host selection logic. Returns presented (human-readable) trace steps grouped by routing round, along with the routing form submission if one was used. If no routing trace exists for the booking, empty steps and groups are returned.  If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `BOOKING_READ` scope is required.

calculate.description: Calculate slots based on routing form response. It will not actually save the response just return the routed event type and slots when it can be booked. The routing form response, as a map of field identifier to answer. Answers use the option label, not the option id. Must not be empty - without answers no route can match.

By usernames only (used for dynamic event type - there is no specific event but you want to know when 2 or more people are available). Example '/v2/slots?usernames=alice,bob&username=bob&organizationSlug=org-slug&start=2033-09-05&end=2033-09-06'. Every version's builder-produced payload carries a `payload.platformOAuthClientId` field naming the owning platform OAuth client (`null` for non-platform events; for the flat-delivered MEETING_STARTED/MEETING_ENDED bodies the field appears at the top level of the body). Zapier deliveries, custom payload templates that do not reference the field, the `AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` / `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` bodies (delivered verbatim from the fire-time blob, never built) and the legacy `FORM_SUBMITTED_NO_EVENT` fallback delivery omit it. Example: 2021-10-20.

create.description: Create a schedule. Create a schedule for the authenticated user. The point of creating schedules is for event types to be available at specific times. The first goal of schedules is to have a default schedule. If you are platform customer and created managed users, then it is important to note that each managed user should have a default schedule. 1. If you passed `timeZone` when creating managed user, then the default schedule from Monday to Friday from 9AM to 5PM will be created with that timezone. The managed user can then change the default schedule via the `AvailabilitySettings` atom. 2. If you did not, then we assume you want the user to have this specific schedule right away. You should create a default schedule by specifying `"isDefault": true` in the request body. Until the user has a default schedule the user can't be booked nor manage their schedule via the AvailabilitySettings atom. The second goal of schedules is to create another schedule that event types can point to. This is useful for when an event is booked because availability is not checked against the default schedule but instead against that specific schedule. After creating a non-default schedule, you can...

get_busy_times.description: Get busy times. Get busy times from a calendar. Example request URL is `https://api.cal.com/v2/calendars/busy-times?timeZone=Europe%2FMadrid&dateFrom=2024-12-18&dateTo=2024-12-18&calendar=135,skrauciz%40gmail.com&calendar=200,bob%40gmail.com`. The `calendar` query parameter identifies one calendar as `<credentialId>,<externalId>`, e.g. `calendar=135,alice@example.com`. Both values are returned for each connected calendar by `GET /v2/calendars`. To load busy times from multiple calendars, pass the `calendar` query parameter multiple times, e.g. `calendar=135,alice@example.com&calendar=200,bob@example.com`. Only the first comma separates the two values, so an `externalId` containing commas is kept intact. Note: loggedInUsersTz is deprecated, use timeZone instead. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `APPS_READ` scope is required. Use `<credentialId>,ics-feed` in `calendar` for an ICS feed, whose address is withheld.

Repeat the parameter to load multiple calendars, e.g. calendar=135,alice@example.com&calendar=200,bob@example.com. At least one calendar is required. Example: ["135,alice@example.com"]. Required here although Cal.com's spec marks it optional: measured 2026-11-23 on two accounts, the call without it answered HTTP 400 and with one calendar answered 200.

list.description: List personal contacts. Returns the authenticated user's personal contacts from their Contacts page, ordered by stored name (nulls last), email and id, with limit/cursor pagination. `contactIds` narrows the list to those contacts, and `tagIds` to contacts carrying at least one of the tags. When pagination.hasMore is true, pass pagination.nextCursor as cursor with the same search, contactIds and tagIds. Use usernames of contacts with groupBooking eligible for dynamic group availability and booking with the authenticated user. Team and organization members are not included. A contact whose email belongs to a verified, discoverable Cal account shows that account's name, username and booking page. Contact avatars and Cal user ids are never returned. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_READ` scope is required. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields.

search.description: Part of a contact's name or email, to narrow the list. Example: jamie.

items.description: Cal.com format: uuid.

contactIds.description: Contact ids from an earlier `GET /v2/contacts`, to list only those contacts. Separate ids with commas, or repeat the parameter once per id. Example: ["0192f3a1-7c2b-7d4e-9a10-000000000001","0192f3a1-7c2b-7d4e-9a10-000000000002"].

items.description: Cal.com format: uuid.

tagIds.description: Tag ids from `GET /v2/contacts/tags`, to list only contacts carrying at least one of them. Separate ids with commas, or repeat the parameter once per id. Example: ["0192f3a1-7c2b-7d4e-9a10-00000000000a","0192f3a1-7c2b-7d4e-9a10-00000000000b"].

limit.description: Maximum number of contacts to return. Default: 50. Example: 50.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page; keep the same search, contactIds and tagIds on subsequent pages.

add.description: Add a personal contact. Adds a personal contact to the authenticated user's Contacts page by email, with an optional name. The email is checked for its format and mail server first, and a user holds at most 5,000 contacts. Adding an email already in the user's contacts changes nothing, not even its name. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required.

email.description: The email address to add. It is checked for its format and mail server, and stored lowercased. Example: jamie.rivera@example.com.

name.description: The contact's name. Leave out when there is none. Example: Jamie Rivera.

get_history.description: Get a personal contact's meeting history. Returns the authenticated user's meeting history with one of their personal contacts, as the contact drawer on the Contacts page shows it: a summary and the meetings of one `status`, 20 per page: `upcoming` soonest first, or `past` newest first. When pagination.hasMore is true, pass pagination.nextCursor as cursor with the same status. Only bookings the user hosts or attends are read, from `summary.coveredSince` onwards (3 months, or less for users with the most bookings). On a seated event the user doesn't host, other seat holders are matched only when the event shows its attendees. Cal Event bookings are left out. The contact's name, email and private note, other attendees, descriptions, locations and booking responses are never returned. A contact the user does not have is not found. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_READ` and `BOOKING_READ` scopes are both required.

status.description: Which meetings to list: `upcoming` soonest first, or `past` newest first, from `summary.coveredSince` onwards. Example: past.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page; keep the same status on subsequent pages.

get_note.description: Get a personal contact's note. Returns the authenticated user's private note on one of their personal contacts, as the contact drawer on the Contacts page shows it, or null when there is none. The note is never returned by `GET /v2/contacts` or any other list. Change it with `note` on `PATCH /v2/contacts/{id}`. A contact the user does not have is not found. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_READ` scope is required.

list_tags.description: List contact tags. Returns the authenticated user's own tags, the ones they can put on their contacts, ordered by name and id, with limit/cursor pagination. Each tag has how many of the user's contacts carry it. They are the same personal tags the user can put on their own links; team tags are not included. When pagination.hasMore is true, pass pagination.nextCursor as cursor. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_READ` scope is required. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields.

limit.description: Maximum number of tags to return. Default: 50. Example: 50.

cursor.description: The pagination.nextCursor value from the previous page. Omit for the first page. Cal.com format: uuid.

create_tag.description: Create a contact tag. Creates one of the authenticated user's own tags, to put on their contacts with `POST /v2/contacts/{id}/tags`. The tag is personal, never a team's, and it is also offered for the user's own links. It does not put the tag on any contact. A name the user already has is refused. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required.

color.description: A hex color. Leave out for the default. Example: #0ea5e9.

update.description: Update a personal contact. Updates one of the authenticated user's personal contacts, changing only the fields given in the body; a body with no fields changes nothing and returns the contact as it is. `note` replaces the user's private note on the contact, sanitized and limited as on the Contacts page, and an empty `note` clears it; read it with `GET /v2/contacts/{id}/note`. A contact on Cal (`type: calUser`) shows the name from their Cal account and can't have its name changed, but it can have a note; a body with both is refused whole and stores neither. A contact the user does not have is not found. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required. Published nullable fields cannot be cleared to null through this connector.

name.description: The contact's new name. A contact on Cal (`type: calUser`) can't have its name changed. Example: Jamie R..

note.description: The user's private note on the contact, which replaces the stored note. To add to it, read it with `GET /v2/contacts/{id}/note` and send the whole new note. An empty string clears it. It is trimmed, and scripts and event handlers are removed, as on the Contacts page. Any contact can have a note, including one on Cal. This connector cannot clear this field to null. Example: Prefers a scissor cut on top, short back and sides. Wants a #2 fade..

remove.description: Remove a personal contact. Removes one of the authenticated user's personal contacts, with its tags. It cannot be undone: adding the email again makes a new contact, without the old one's tags. A contact the user does not have is not found. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required.

add_tag.description: Add a tag to a contact. Puts one of the authenticated user's own tags on one of their contacts. The contact keeps every other tag, and a tag it already carries is left as it is. A team tag, another user's tag or an unknown id is refused. A contact the user does not have is not found. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required. Cal.com validates input formats described on the fields.

tagId.description: The id of one of the user's own tags, from `GET /v2/contacts/tags`. Cal.com format: uuid. Example: 0192f3a1-7c2b-7d4e-9a10-00000000000a.

remove_tag.description: Remove a tag from a contact. Takes one tag off one of the authenticated user's contacts. The contact keeps every other tag, and a tag it does not carry changes nothing. The tag itself is not deleted. A contact the user does not have is not found. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required.

tagId.description: The tag's `id` from the contact's `tags`. Example: 0192f3a1-7c2b-7d4e-9a10-00000000000a.

list_suggestions.description: List suggested contacts. Returns people the authenticated user keeps meeting but hasn't added as personal contacts: people the user met at least 4 times in the last 12 months, adding up the accepted, past bookings the user hosted that they attended, the accepted, past bookings the user attended that they hosted, and the past, non-cancelled Cal Events the user hosted that they were a confirmed guest of. Existing contacts, the user's own emails, teammates (users who share an accepted team or organization membership with the user), dismissed suggestions and blocked emails are left out. Ordered by meeting count, then most recent meeting, with limit/cursor pagination; when pagination.hasMore is true, pass pagination.nextCursor as cursor. To accept a suggestion, add it with `POST /v2/contacts` using its email and name. To hide it for good, dismiss it with `POST /v2/contacts/suggestions/dismissals`. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_READ` scope is required.

limit.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return. Default: 50. Example: 50.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from pagination.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

dismiss_suggestion.description: Dismiss a suggested contact. Stops suggesting an email to the authenticated user, for good. Dismissing an email that was already dismissed, or that isn't suggested, changes nothing. It does not add or remove a personal contact; to accept a suggestion instead, use `POST /v2/contacts`. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `CONTACT_WRITE` scope is required.

email.description: The suggestion's email from `GET /v2/contacts/suggestions`. It is matched without regard to case or surrounding spaces. Example: jamie.rivera@example.com.

list.description: List Events (cursor pagination). Returns the Events the authenticated user hosts: Events they own, plus Events they have accepted a co-host invitation to. A co-hosted Event may be owned by a team, so a team-owned Event can appear here — but team-owned Events the user neither hosts nor co-hosts are not returned by this endpoint; list those with `GET /v2/teams/{teamId}/events`. Ordered by start time, newest first when `status` is omitted. Use cursor-based pagination: pass `pagination.nextCursor` from a previous response as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page; omit `cursor` for the first page. `pagination.hasMore` is `false` and `pagination.nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.  Events are fixed-date RSVP pages served at cal.com/{slug}; they are not event types (bookable meeting templates) or calendar events. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_READ` scope is required.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for cursor-based pagination. Pass the `pagination.nextCursor` value from a previous response to fetch the next page. Omit to fetch the first page. Example: eyJ2IjoyLCJzdGFydFRpbWUiOiIyMDMwLTAxLTAxVDAwOjAwOjAwLjAwMFoiLCJldmVudFR5cGVVdWlkIjoiMDE4ZjRjMmUtM2YxYS03YWJjLTlkZWYtMDEyMzQ1Njc4OWFiIn0.

limit.description: Maximum number of Events to return. Default: 50. Example: 25.

slug.description: Filter by the event's public page slug (cal.com/{slug}). Example: team-offsite.

status.description: Filter events by lifecycle status. `draft`: not published and not cancelled, ordered soonest first. `upcoming`: published and not yet ended, or cancelled but not yet started, ordered soonest first. `past`: everything else, ordered latest first. Omit to return all statuses, newest first. When provided, `pagination.nextCursor` encodes the status — cursors from one status value cannot be used with another and return 400. Example: upcoming.

create.description: Create an Event. Creates a draft Event for the authenticated user. A draft is not public and nobody can register until it is published with `POST /v2/events/{uuid}/publish`. To create an Event owned by a team, use `POST /v2/teams/{teamId}/events`. `startTime` and `endTime` are ISO 8601 in UTC; `startTime` must not be in the past and `endTime` must be after `startTime`. `guestList` controls whether guests see names, a count, or neither. `locations` sets where the Event happens; set `price` and `currency` on a location to charge for that place. Events are fixed-date RSVP pages served at cal.com/{slug}; they are not event types (bookable meeting templates) or calendar events. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_WRITE` scope is required. Published nullable fields cannot be cleared to null through this connector. registrationFields[] has Cal.com-validated object variants. registrationFields[] must omit showWhen. locations[] has Cal.com-validated object variants.

title.description: The Event's title. Example: Team offsite.

startTime.description: When the Event starts, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. It must not be in the past. Example: 2030-01-01T10:00:00.000Z.

endTime.description: When the Event ends, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. It must be after `startTime`. Example: 2030-01-01T11:00:00.000Z.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone the Event's times are shown in. Example: Europe/Berlin.

slug.description: Public page slug (cal.com/{slug}): 10-100 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Generated from the title when omitted. Example: team-offsite-2030.

description.description: What the Event is about, shown on its page. This connector cannot clear this field to null.

visibility.description: Once published: PUBLIC is listed on the owner's page, UNLISTED only opens from its link. Defaults to PUBLIC. Default: PUBLIC.

capacity.description: The most guests the Event can take. Omit for unlimited. Ignored once any location has its own `capacity`: the Event then takes the sum of the location capacities, or is unlimited if any location has none. The waitlist only opens when the Event or the chosen location is full, so it only works when capacity is set on the Event or on a location. This connector cannot clear this field to null.

waitlistEnabled.description: Let guests join a waitlist when the Event is full. The waitlist only opens when the Event or the chosen location is full, so it only works when capacity is set on the Event or on a location. Default: false.

paymentTimeoutMinutes.description: How many minutes a guest's seat is held while they pay. This connector cannot clear this field to null.

registrationOpensAt.description: When guests can start registering, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must be before registration closes. This connector cannot clear this field to null. Example: 2029-12-01T09:00:00.000Z.

registrationClosesAt.description: When registration closes, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must not be after `startTime`. Guests already on the waitlist can still be promoted after it closes. This connector cannot clear this field to null. Example: 2029-12-31T12:00:00.000Z.

requiresApproval.description: Registrations wait for a host's approval. Default: false.

showOrganizerEmail.description: Show the organizer's email to guests. Default: true.

guestList.description: Who guests can see on the Event's page. `names` lists them, `count` shows how many, `hidden` shows neither. Defaults to `names`. Default: names.

showPresentedBy.description: Show who the Event is presented by. Default: true.

theme.description: Default theme of the event page. This connector cannot clear this field to null.

colors.description: Exactly three hex colors the effect is drawn with. Example: ["#0b1c2c","#1f6feb","#a5d8ff"].

get_listings.description: Get Discover listings by id. Returns published Discover listings by id, with the fields their public cards show: service name, provider, price, new-client discount, the provider's rating, review count and verification, duration, whether it is online, city, neighborhood and the business's time zone. With `includeNextAvailable`, also the earliest open slot in the next 7 days for the first 10 listings. Any id that is not a published listing is returned in `notFoundListingIds`. Requests with `includeNextAvailable` are limited to 60 per minute per user, shared across all of the user's API keys and access tokens. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

ids.description: Discover listing ids, such as the `listingId` values a Discover search returned. Repeat the parameter (`ids=12&ids=34`) or separate the ids with commas (`ids=12,34`). Duplicates are read once. Example: [12,34].

includeNextAvailable.description: Also look up each listing's earliest open slot in the next 7 days. Only the first 10 listings are checked, so list the ones you care about first. Default: false. Example: true.

search_listings.description: Search Discover listings. Searches the published Discover listings the way Cal.ai does. In-person results stay within the area you name, else around your saved ZIP code; with neither, nothing is searched and `areaNeeded` is returned. When the named area or the saved ZIP code cannot be found, nothing is searched and `areaNeeded` comes with `areaNotFound`. Online-only categories and `onlineOnly` searches are searched everywhere. An empty neighborhood widens to its whole region (`widenedFrom`); an empty search retries with the category alone (`broadenedFrom`); when the whole area has nothing, the web is searched there once and businesses not on Discover come back in `webBusinesses`. Availability is judged in your saved time zone. Searches are limited to 20 per minute per user, and web searches to 10 per hour per user, each shared across all of the user's API keys and access tokens; past the web search limit a search still returns its listings, without `webBusinesses`. The web search runs on your own AI access: when one of your organizations has turned AI off, it is skipped and the listings still return. A place lookup that is rate limited answers 429 and one that fails answers 503,...

category.description: The Discover category the need maps to, such as `medical` for tooth pain. Example: barbers.

subcategory.description: A subcategory of `category`, such as `dentistry` under `medical`. Ignored without its category, and named in `ignoredFilters` when it is not one of the category's. Example: haircuts.

query.description: Free text matched against the title, description, provider and subcategory. Never a place. Example: skin fade.

neighborhood.description: A neighborhood of a launch region, such as `Capitol Hill`, for in-person listings there only. An unknown name comes back in `ignoredFilters`. Example: Capitol Hill.

onlineOnly.description: Keep only online listings and search them everywhere, whatever `area` says. Online searches never fall back to the web. Example: false.

localQuery.description: For the web fallback, the need in the area's local language when it is not English, such as `Zahnarzt` for a dentist in Hamburg. Example: Zahnarzt.

area.description: The place to search around: a ZIP code, neighborhood or city. Without it, the search uses your saved ZIP code, and answers `areaNeeded` when there is none. Pass `anywhere` for results from anywhere. Example: 98122.

maximumPrice.description: The highest price, in whole currency units: 50 means $50, 0 means free only. Example: 50.

maximumDurationMinutes.description: The longest session, in minutes. Example: 60.

availableWithin.description: Only listings with a real open slot in this window, in your saved time zone. `this_week` means the next 7 days. Example: today.

call_business.description: Call a web-found business to book. Has Cal's voice assistant call a business on the user's behalf to book the service, the way Cal.ai does once the user approves. Only a business that `GET /v2/discover/listings/search` returned in `webBusinesses` to this same user in the last 24 hours can be called, with its URL exactly as returned; a Discover listing is never called, because it is booked from its `bookingUrl`. Every check runs before the call: the account may place calls, the business's page offers a US or Canadian appointment phone, the name and service are plain words, the business was not called too recently, and the user's plan covers it. The call is placed by Cal's AI voice assistant, so a user in an organization that opted out of AI cannot place calls. A call that is not placed answers `placed: false` with the `reason`. A refusal spends neither daily limit, except a refusal for calling hours found after Cal set up the call, which keeps that business's count for the day. If dialling fails after the call was started, the user's call is given back when the provider refused the dial, but that business's count for the day is... Cal.com may charge credits at an unpublished price.

businessUrl.description: The business's URL, exactly as a `search_listings` web business gave it in `webBusinesses[].url`. Only a business found by your own search in the last 24 hours can be called. Example: https://barbers.example/book.

service.description: What to book, in plain words, such as `upright piano full tuning and pitch raise`. Put when the user can come in `timing`, the staff member they asked for in `staff` and their booking details in `notes`. Never put contact details (phone, email, address) in it. Example: upright piano full tuning and pitch raise.

timing.description: When the user can come, in their words, such as `Thursday after 5 or Friday morning`. Leave it out when they named no window. Never put contact details in it. Example: Thursday after 5 or Friday morning.

staff.description: The staff member the user asked for, in their words, such as `Sam`. Leave it out when they named none; never take one from the business's page. Example: Sam.

notes.description: Booking details the user gave for this booking, such as `allergic to lavender`. Only what they said, never contact details. Leave it out when they gave none. Example: allergic to lavender.

daysFromToday.description: The day the user asked for, in days from today in their saved time zone: 0 today, 1 tomorrow. Cal asks the business for that date. Leave it out when the user named no day. Example: 1.

callerName.description: The name the user gave for themselves, which Cal gives on the call. Leave it out to use the account name; never a name from a search result. Example: Jamie Rivera.

book_business.description: Book a web-found business online. Has Cal's booking agent book a service on a business's own online booking page for the user, the way Cal.ai does once the user approves. Only a business that `GET /v2/discover/listings/search` returned in `webBusinesses` to this same user in the last 24 hours can be booked, with its URL exactly as returned; a Discover listing is never booked this way, because it is booked from its `bookingUrl`. Every check runs before the job starts: the account may book online, has a username, has fewer than the allowed number of jobs running, and its plan covers the booking. The booking agent browses with AI, so a user in an organization that opted out of AI cannot book online. A job that is not started answers `created: false` with the `reason` and spends no budget. A started job answers with `jobUrl`, the job's page, where the user picks an appointment option, approves the price and terms, or cancels: this API never chooses or approves anything. Every request carries an `idempotencyKey` the client generates once per booking; send the same key to retry the same request and get the same job back without spend... Cal.com may charge credits at an unpublished price.

businessUrl.description: The business's URL, exactly as a `search_listings` web business gave it in `webBusinesses[].url`. Only a business found by your own search in the last 24 hours can be booked. Example: https://barbers.example/book.

service.description: What to book, in plain words, such as `haircut`. Example: haircut.

area.description: The user's area as they gave it: a ZIP code, neighborhood or city. Example: Capitol Hill, Seattle.

daysFromToday.description: The day the user asked for, in days from today in their saved time zone: `0` today, `1` tomorrow. Example: 1.

partOfDay.description: The part of that day the user asked for, on the business's local clock; `any` when they did not say. Example: afternoon.

budgetDollars.description: The most the user wants to pay for the service, in US dollars, when they said so. Example: 60.

idempotencyKey.description: A key you generate once per booking, such as a UUID. Send the same key to retry the same request: you get its job back, and no second job starts. Example: 4b7d1c2e-9f0a-4e1b-8c3d-2a6f5e7d9b10.

create_service_request.description: Ask to be told when a Discover provider joins. Records that the authenticated user is looking for a service Discover has no listing for, so they are emailed at their account address when a matching provider joins. Asking again for the same need within 90 days returns the open request only in the same region: a repeat in another region, or with a `searchedArea` where there was none (or none where there was one), records a new request. `matchedProviders` in the response says which new providers can trigger the email: only online ones, or none, when the request is outside every launch region, so pass the `searchedArea` of the user's search. The response never includes the request's id, an email address or who else asked. Limited to 10 requests per hour per user, shared across all of the user's API keys and access tokens. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `PROFILE_WRITE` scope is required.

service.description: The service in two or three words, as a provider would list it, such as dentist or piano lessons. Never the user's own words or personal details. Example: piano lessons.

category.description: The Discover category it belongs to. Example: lessons.

subcategory.description: The subcategory slug within that category, when one fits. A subcategory outside the category is ignored. Example: music-and-voice.

searchedArea.description: The `searchedArea` a `search_listings` (`GET /v2/discover/listings/search`) result returned when it found nothing, copied as given; it decides the region the request is matched in, and a repeat returns the open request only from the same region. Leave it out when there was none. Example: within 10 miles of Seattle, WA.
